title: Funding Austin's Future: Safety & Air Travel
summary:
*   Austin officials convened to discuss the city's financial priorities, focusing on budget proposals for the upcoming fiscal year.
*   Key briefings covered funding for essential public safety services, including the Fire Department, EMS, and Police.
*   Discussions also included budget allocations for the Municipal Court system and airport operations.
*   This session was part of the preparatory work for the city's 2002-2003 budget, setting the stage for future financial decisions.
transcript:
MINUTES OF CITY COUNCIL WORKSESSION 
AUGUST 7,2002
Austin City Council
MINUTES
WORKSESSION
WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 7,2002
The following represents the actions taken by the Austin City Council in the order they occurred
during the meeting. While the minutes are not in sequential order, all agenda items were discussed.
The City Council of Austin, Texas convened in a Work Session on Wednesday, August 7, 2002 at
One Texas Center, 505 Barton Springs Road, third floor training room, Austin, Texas.
Mayor Garcia called the meeting to order at 10:09 a.m.
Budget Briefings - Fiscal Year 2002-2003
1. 
Protective Services: Fire, EMS, Police and Municipal Court
The presentation was made by: Laura Huffman, Assistant City Manager, Protective
Services; Richard Herrington, Director, EMS; Dr. Ed Racht, Medical Director, EMS;
Chief Gary Warren, Austin Fire Department; Assistant Chief Paul Maldonado, Austin Fire
Department; Chief Stan Knee, Austin Police Department; and Judge Evelyn McKee,
Presiding Judge, Municipal Court.
2. 
Enterprise Services: Aviation, Convention and Solid Waste Services
The presentation was made by: Jim Smith, Director, Aviation; and Charles Gates,
Director, Financial and Administrative Services.
The presentation by the Convention Center and Solid Waste Services will be at the regular meeting
of Council on Thursday, August 8,2002.
The motion to adjourn the meeting at 12:10 p.m. was approved on Council Member Slusher's
motion, Council Member Alvarez' second on a 6-0 vote with Council Member Dunkerley off the
dais.
The minutes from the work session of August 7, 2002 and regular meeting of August 8, 2002 were
approved on Council Member Thomas' motion, Council Member Wynn's second on a 7-0 vote.
